messages:
sam: heads up — deploybot started an engine bundle swap to kernel-quant:v4-rc3 in the night window (us-west-2). canary slice 5% just flipped. seeing a handful of OOM spikes in the first 10m :eyes:
jun: copying telemetry now. can you paste the deploybot status?
sam: sure — output below:
```
deploybot status --id=rb-20260321-34
state: rolling
progress: 5% (canary)
variants: kernel-quant:v4-rc3 -> kernel-quant:v3-stable (fallback)
errors: 7 OOMs / 12m across 3 hosts
notes: matmul-v2 kernel used, q4-opt quant path
```
deploybot: [automated] operation rb-20260321-34: shard allocation applied, slow rollback threshold set to 10 errors / 5m.
elaine: hmm — 7 OOMs in 12m at 5% is concerning. suggest we pin traffic immediately and open for investigation. i recommend: pin TTL=24h, abort further slices until we confirm.
ryan: +1 for pin. rollback latency is ~3m if we flip routing, but we need to ensure no autoscale churn. if we pin, ops will run a dry rollback sweep after pin to validate path.
maria: can we get a quick signal check? cpu/gpu mem high? also which models hit the OOMs (long context vs perf tests)?
jun: looking — majority from long-context evals hitting seq_len ~12k on a3g-large. mem blowups around kv-cache growth. thermal traces show modest increase but not enough to explain immediate OOM. attaching short trace: `oom@kernel: alloc 1.8G -> fail`
sam: tying to reproduce in staging — matmul-v2 quant path differs from v3 shim. could be an allocation path regression. i want to avoid a wide rollback without a minimal root cause.
elaine: i still think pin now, investigate after. public-facing SLAs — we should avoid more errors.
release-bot: release notes draft created: https://internal.redwood/release/engine/kernel-quant-v4-rc3 (auto) — added canary note and rollback steps.
jun: ops checks: `kubectl get pods -l role=engine` shows two hosts with repeated restart counts. i'll cordon the hosts used in canary slice to prevent further user traffic.
ryan: cordon sounds good, but be mindful that dedicated pools shared with Dedicated customers — coordinate with cs if we see customer impact.
maria: quick remediation checklist:
- pin routing to kernel-quant:v3-stable (temporary)
- cordon affected hosts (jun)
- collect full kv-cache dumps from the two hosts
- run matmul regression proto on staging with exact quant flags
- hold release notes update until we confirm root cause

sam: action: i'll request pin now. pinging @deploybot to apply pin with TTL=24h.
deploybot: [action] pin-request accepted. applying pin: kernel-quant -> v3-stable, ttl=24h. roll signal: HOLD.
elaine: thanks. once pin is on, can we run a limited rollforward test with matmul-v2 but q3-compat quant flags to isolate quant path?
jun: yes — i'll spin a 1-node staging job with `--quant-path=q3-compat --matmul=matmul-v2` and run the failing evals. i'll post logs in this thread.
sam: appreciate it. also update the release notes: mark the night window attempt as aborted and note OOM investigation. release-bot — can you add the aborted flag?
release-bot: release notes updated (status: aborted-canary). link: https://internal.redwood/release/engine/kernel-quant-v4-rc3#notes
ryan: quick reminder — if pin TTL expires and we still haven't resolved, ops will automatically unpin. set a calendar reminder for EOD triage if needed.
maria: adding a short runbook snippet here for oncall:
- if >10 errors/5m: pin immediately
- cordon hosts with >3 restarts
- run `kv-dump --host` and upload to /infra/kv-dumps/
- revert to v3-stable traffic if reproduction within 30m

sam: thanks everyone. jun, post the staging reproducer logs when ready and i'll coordinate rollback if we see repro. :thumbsup:
jun: will post in ~12m — starting the job now.
deploybot: [automated] pin applied successfully. traffic now routed to kernel-quant:v3-stable.
sam: verified routing shift in metrics — error rate dropped to baseline within 2m. leaving pin for 24h per TTL.
elaine: good. we'll loop in research tomorrow to check quant build flags and matmul kernel differences.
ryan: noted for CS. i'll file a short incident note for the dedicated customers touched.
maria: great. follow-ups: jun will paste logs, sam will draft a short postmortem if we confirm regression, ops will keep pin until EOD triage.
sam: closing the thread for now — will reopen if staging shows repro. thanks all.
